message.reasoning_content:
Analyze this reduced C/C++ function. It may or may not contain a vulnerability.
Reply with single best line number where primary bug is introduced.

Function appends quoted token. Uses strlcat and strncat. strncat will stop at NUL? strncat copies up to n bytes but stops at NUL? Actually strncat copies at most n chars, but stops at NUL. Wait strncat spec: copies at most n characters from src, not including terminating NUL? It stops at NUL. So embedded NUL bytes in tok_len will be truncated. Also strlcat expects null-terminated dest. But main issue: strncat(sql, tok, tok_len) will not copy embedded NULs correctly? strncat will stop at first NUL in tok, so len may include embedded NUL, but strncat will stop early. Also strlcat after may be okay.

But also strlcat(sql, "'", sql_cap) assumes sql is null-terminated and has space. No check.

Primary bug is line 5: strncat with tok_len but tok may contain NUL, strncat stops early, also strncat doesn't respect len for non-null-terminated? Actually strncat will copy up to tok_len bytes but stops at first NUL. So embedded NUL lost. Also strncat expects src null-terminated. If tok_len includes embedded NUL, the source is not null-terminated at that point? It may be.

Better bug: strncat does not guarantee to copy exactly tok_len bytes; it stops at NUL. So vulnerability is line 5.

Also strlcat on line 4 and 6 may overflow? strlcat is safe.

Maybe bug is using strncat with len that may include NUL, leading to truncation and missing closing quote? Actually closing quote still added.

Primary bug introduced at line 5.

Answer: 5
